beautician = a person who gives beauty treatments such as facials and nails
call-out charge = a fee for a worker to come to your home, before any repair
hourly rate = the amount a worker charges for each hour of work
quote = a written price offered for a job before the work begins
gratuity = money given to staff for good service, sometimes added to a bill
tradesperson = a skilled worker such as a plumber, electrician or carpenter
boycott = refusing to buy from a company as a protest
impulse buy = something you buy suddenly without planning
planned obsolescence = designing goods to wear out or go out of date so people buy again
ethical shopping = choosing goods made without harm to people, animals or the planet
ethically sourced = obtained in a way that treats workers and producers fairly
sweatshop = a factory with very poor pay and conditions
shopaholic = a person who cannot stop buying things, even if they do not need them
retail therapy = buying things in order to cheer yourself up
designer label = clothes or goods with a famous fashion designer's name
own-brand = a product sold under the supermarket's own name, usually cheaper
upmarket = intended for richer customers; high quality and expensive
mass-produced = made in large numbers by machines, not by hand
throwaway society = a culture that throws things away instead of repairing them
consumerism = the idea that buying more and more goods is a good way to live
